# Generate a 4:3 PowerPoint deck from the report figures

This script reuses the exact data-loading and plotting code from
`channel_fisheries_combined_report.Rmd` via a small `run_chunk()` helper — every
`run_chunk("label")` call below extracts and evaluates that chunk's **real,
unmodified code** straight from the main report. Nothing is retyped or duplicated.

**Before running:** knit (or at least run) the main report once so that
`output/cache/*.RData` exist. This script loads those caches directly — it does
not need the raw AER Excel file or GFW pipeline `.RData` files to be present,
only the cache.

Save this file in the **same folder** as `channel_fisheries_combined_report.Rmd`
(or edit `main_rmd` below), then knit or run chunk-by-chunk.

```{r packages}
library(tidyverse)
library(officer)
library(sf)
library(spatstat)
library(rnaturalearth)
library(rnaturalearthdata)
library(ineq)
library(patchwork)
library(scales)
```

```{r register-chunks}
# Path to the main report Rmd
main_rmd <- "channel_fisheries_combined_report.Rmd"

if (!file.exists(main_rmd)) {
  stop("Cannot find '", main_rmd,
       "'. Place this script in the same folder as the main report, ",
       "or edit `main_rmd` to the correct path.")
}

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# NOTE ON IMPLEMENTATION: knitr::read_chunk() is NOT used here.
# read_chunk() scans the *entire* source file (including prose) with a
# regex-based chunk-boundary matcher, and on reports with very long lines of
# prose (some paragraphs in the literature/discussion sections exceed 1000
# characters) this can trigger a "node stack overflow" in R's PCRE engine.
# extract_chunk() below does a simple, single-pass line scan instead — it
# only looks for chunk fences and label headers, never runs a regex over
# whole-paragraph text, and cannot suffer the same failure mode.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

extract_chunk <- function(filepath, label) {
  lines <- readLines(filepath, warn = FALSE)

  fence_re <- "^```\\{r[ ]+([a-zA-Z0-9_.-]+)"
  start_idx <- NA_integer_

  for (i in seq_along(lines)) {
    if (grepl("^```\\{r", lines[i], fixed = FALSE)) {
      m <- regmatches(lines[i], regexpr(fence_re, lines[i]))
      if (length(m) > 0) {
        this_label <- sub(fence_re, "\\1", m)
        if (identical(this_label, label)) {
          start_idx <- i
          break
        }
      }
    }
  }

  if (is.na(start_idx)) {
    stop("Chunk '", label, "' not found in ", filepath)
  }

  # Find the closing ``` fence after start_idx
  end_idx <- NA_integer_
  for (j in seq(start_idx + 1, length(lines))) {
    if (identical(trimws(lines[j]), "```")) {
      end_idx <- j
      break
    }
  }
  if (is.na(end_idx)) {
    stop("Closing fence for chunk '", label, "' not found in ", filepath)
  }

  paste(lines[(start_idx + 1):(end_idx - 1)], collapse = "\n")
}

# run_chunk(): extracts a chunk's code and evaluates it in the calling
# (global) environment, so subsequent chunks see the same objects exactly
# as if the code had been pasted inline.
#
# IMPORTANT: a plain eval(parse(...)) does NOT auto-print top-level visible
# results the way the R console does, which means a chunk ending in a bare
# ggplot pipe (no explicit print()) would never register with last_plot().
# To replicate console behaviour, each parsed expression is evaluated with
# withVisible() and explicitly print()'d when visible — this is exactly what
# let's a trailing `... |> ggplot(...) + ...` show up in last_plot().
run_chunk <- function(label, filepath = main_rmd) {
  code  <- extract_chunk(filepath, label)
  exprs <- parse(text = code)
  for (e in exprs) {
    res <- withVisible(eval(e, envir = .GlobalEnv))
    if (res$visible) print(res$value)
  }
  invisible(NULL)
}
```

<!-- ===========================================================
     PPTX SETUP
     =========================================================== -->

```{r pptx-settings}
pptx_path <- file.path(out_dir, "channel_fisheries_figures.pptx")

# 4:3 slide geometry (inches)
slide_w <- 10
slide_h <- 7.5
margin  <- 0.3
max_w   <- slide_w - 2*margin
max_h   <- slide_h - 2*margin

# Adds one ggplot/patchwork object as a full-bleed image slide, scaled to fit
# within the slide while preserving its aspect ratio. No PowerPoint title
# placeholder is added — every figure already carries its own title via
# ggplot's labs(title = ...), so a redundant slide title is omitted.
add_plot_slide <- function(doc, plot_obj, width_in = 8, height_in = 5) {

  doc <- add_slide(doc, layout = "Blank", master = "Office Theme")

  tmp_png <- tempfile(fileext = ".png")
  ggsave(tmp_png, plot = plot_obj, width = width_in, height = height_in,
         dpi = 220, units = "in", bg = "white")

  asp <- width_in / height_in
  if (max_w / max_h > asp) {
    draw_h <- max_h
    draw_w <- max_h * asp
  } else {
    draw_w <- max_w
    draw_h <- max_w / asp
  }
  pos_x <- (slide_w - draw_w) / 2
  pos_y <- (slide_h - draw_h) / 2

  ph_with(doc, value = external_img(tmp_png, width = draw_w, height = draw_h),
          location = ph_location(left = pos_x, top = pos_y,
                                  width = draw_w, height = draw_h))
}

# 4:3 PowerPoint base document. If your local officer template defaults to
# 16:9, supply a blank 4:3 .potx via `read_pptx(path = "template_4x3.potx")`
# instead — see Annex note in the main report for where to source one.
pptx <- read_pptx()
```

```{r slide-title}
pptx <- add_slide(pptx, layout = "Title Slide", master = "Office Theme")
pptx <- ph_with(pptx, value = "Fishing in the English Channel",
                 location = ph_location_type(type = "ctrTitle"))
pptx <- ph_with(pptx,
                 value = "Trends in Fishing Effort, Landings and Spatial Distributions \u2014 STECF AER & GFW",
                 location = ph_location_type(type = "subTitle"))
```

# Figure 16 is a patchwork object (p_gini + p_top10 via plot_annotation()).
# ggsave() handles patchwork objects the same way as plain ggplot objects,
# and last_plot() captures the most recently *printed* plot — patchwork
# objects auto-print at the end of the chunk just like ggplot objects do.
pptx <- add_plot_slide(pptx, last_plot(), width_in = 9, height_in = 4)
